## Film vs. Digital: The /gg/ War Continues

The decade-long turf war on 4chan’s /gg/ board shows no signs of abating. A recent thread has reignited the debate between film purists and digital enthusiasts, centering on the strawman character "cANON." Purists argue that true photographic mastery requires sticking to low ISO film (ISO 200 or less) and avoiding the noise inherent in high-ISO digital sensors. They contend that significant photographic works were captured with ISO 100 or lower, contrasting this with "digislugs" who rely on wide apertures and post-processing to achieve equivalence.

Defending the digital camp, user cANON highlighted the dynamic range (DR) advantages of modern full-frame sensors and the reach benefits of APS-C bodies like the Canon 90D. The debate grew heated when older posters mocked cANON’s claim that "I'll fix it in post," suggesting that high-ISO digital images result in inferior "clanker abominations." The core sentiment remains a skepticism toward raw resolution numbers, with participants arguing that base ISO saturation and aperture mechanics remain the true drivers of quality.

## Brazil’s iGaming Ban Enforces October 6

A major legislative shift has occurred in South America as Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva officially banned betting companies from operating in the country. According to iGaming Business, the enforcement date is set for October 6. This move under Lula’s administration aims to tighten state control over the gambling sector.

The announcement has sparked discussion on Hacker News, where users are analyzing the ripple effects on the local iGaming market. While the initial reports are brief, the consensus indicates a significant policy change that will force many online betting operators to either exit the Brazilian market or adapt their operations to meet new regulatory standards.

## Sony Community Welcomes New Users

In a more celebratory vein, the Sony Alpha community is seeing a surge of welcoming posts for users with FE/E Mount, A Mount, and legacy Minolta gear. Discussions have focused on the accessible entry points into the ecosystem, with the Sony a6000 being a frequent highlight. Users shared experiences with specific lens combinations, such as the Sony 55-210mm and the Sigma 30mm f/1.4.

Unlike the technical debates seen elsewhere, the sentiment here is inclusive. Users like KickinAP1985 and pancheats shared personal photos taken with these setups, focusing on the joy of creation and equipment sharing rather than pixel-peeping or spec wars. It serves as a reminder of the hobbyist side of photography that often gets lost in the gear-head discourse.

## Gaming Crossovers and Marathon Streams

The gaming world is buzzing with crossover excitement. Twitch streamer @sebmal is currently hosting "The Mareepathon 2," a 24+ hour marathon of the *Pokémon* Channel minigame "Mareep Farm." The stream features a unique mechanic where subscriptions extend the runtime, with multi-subs doubling the time added. Community members have even created exclusive animated emotes to support the broadcast.

Simultaneously, fans are reacting to the collaborative trailer for *Monster Hunter Rise*, which features a crossover with *Sonic the Hedgehog* for the Nintendo Switch. Meanwhile, @1UpGaming highlighted the release of *Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds*, emphasizing its multi-dimensional gameplay across land, sea, air, space, and time, available on both the current Switch and the upcoming Switch 2.

## LLMs as Executive Function Aids

A nuanced discussion on Bluesky has emerged regarding the utility of Large Language Models for neurodivergent individuals, particularly those with ADHD. Users describe LLMs not just as chatbots, but as essential productivity tools for managing finances, paperwork, and email. Specific features like "scratch pads" for task switching are cited as magical for maintaining context between disparate work streams. The sentiment is overwhelmingly positive, with many users labeling these AI tools as underrated essentials that solve lifelong struggles with organization and executive function.

***

## Quick Hits

*   **Knives Out Meme:** The "Welcome [Subject]" meme format based on Benoit Blanc’s line continues to trend, with users posting humorous completions ranging from "the weekend" to the abstract "the ah."
*   **JAV Release:** User @JAV Titles highlighted *Deep Keep Dripping Lesbians 5*, focusing on the dynamic between performers Emi Haruna and Aika Otowa.
*   **Space Music:** KVR contributor Benedict released *White World*, a space music album with a "Goth" leaning, produced without AI, loops, or AutoTune.
*   **Idaho Senate:** Todd Achilles is gaining traction as a viable Republican candidate for Idaho’s Senate seat, with users noting his competence on trans rights and fundraising potential compared to incumbent Jim Risch.
*   **Xenosaga Critique:** User @Worth_Mail_3292 critiqued the *Xenosaga* series for superficial use of Nietzschean philosophy, comparing its narrative density to the *Pokémon* Ruby/Sapphire/Emerald trilogy.

@cANON - /p/ — /gg/ - gear general — >>4530646 Because I agree with the general sentiment. Aperture includes aperture and ISO, insecure sensorlets will deny this against all proof. The last part I have disagreements with but it's nuance at that point. Things like ISO setting vs measured ISO muddy things up. Measured ISO is the one you should be using for true equivalence. Claims like "better sensor technology" are questionable at best. FWC only matters if you can saturate it (basically if shooting with plenty of light wide open). Smaller sensor at equivalent settings clips earlier. If you're not flooding the wells at base ISO, FF's DR advantage is mostly gone. But if you have equivalent lengths, FF has a potential for higher resolution. That's a big IF, though. Also a 24MP APS-C body adds no relevant reach to your kit if your FF body is 60MP. You need something like a Canon 90D for something FF can't reach. It won't be a lot but it will be some extra.

clusters.summary: The /gg/ community on 4chan continues its decade-long debate between film purists and digital enthusiasts, specifically targeting the strawman character "cANON" to argue that skilled photographers should stick to low ISO film (ISO 200 or less) and avoid high-ISO digital sensors. Participants assert that all significant photographic works were captured on film with ISO 100 or lower, contrasting this with "digislugs" who rely on high ISO settings and wide apertures to achieve equivalence. cANON defends the digital side by explaining measured ISO, dynamic range (DR) advantages on full-frame sensors, and how smaller APS-C bodies like the Canon 90D offer unique reach advantages over high-resolution 60MP full-frame bodies. Meanwhile, older posters mock cANON’s claim that "I'll fix it in post" for weddings, suggesting that high-ISO digital shots result in inferior "clanker abominations." The thread highlights a persistent skepticism toward claims of superior modern sensor technology, arguing that base ISO saturation and aperture mechanics remain more critical than raw resolution numbers.

representative_texts: @Worth_Mail_3292 - JRPG — What is the "intended" target? Xenosaga vs. Pokémon RSE — The Xenosaga series has games subtitled after works by Nietzsche (except the first, which isn't actually one of his books but an arbitrary posthumous collage of aphorisms drawn from notebooks written across different periods made by his sister), so the work suggests a serious dialogue with the author, unlike, say, pop works that use references in a purely decorative way (like Heidegger in FF7) that promise nothing. However, there are several things that strike me as very superficial, which lead me to think that the very choice of using those subtitles is almost misleading, precisely because it seems to promise something it then fails to deliver. This isn't about agreeing or disagreeing with Nietzsche's thought, but about whether that thought is present in any form within the work itself. I'll note that Takahashi states in an interview: "However, that's merely the way I think about the story. It was deliberately devised not to be highly involved, so anyone should be able to get into it easily." But simplifying means presenting something in a simpler way, the problem here is that there's nothing to simplify.   Regarding Episode I: The definition Takahashi himself gives of the will to power in the same interview: "The people in this game are all living with some past put upon them, filled with regrets and unavoidable destinies. They all need to find their own identity, and they all need to find the power to go on in life. That's the 'desire for power' I wanted to show in this story." already seems like a misleading reading of the original concept, because what he describes is something close to resilience, not an intrinsic and universal property of life as Nietzsche describes it (explicitly distinct from mere self-preservation). And looking at the character arcs in Episode I, I haven't seen a single character that maps onto that concept.   Regarding Episode II: The subtitle "Beyond Good and Evil" is often misread as synonymous with "beyond binary morality", even someone attempting to explain the reference seriously falls into the same common misunderstanding: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/wze48-qX2Vw . The original title actually refers to a precise concept, I'd invite reading the original texts to go deeper, but Nietzsche isn't criticizing morality as a binary structure, he's attacking a specific morality (that of ressentiment). So if we want the more precise reading, it would be "beyond THAT binary morality." Both of Nietzsche's moralities remain binary, what changes is the dynamic and the psychological origin of the distinction. In Episode II there's no trace of any of this.   Regarding Episode III: The eternal recurrence is not only taken in its philosophically weakest version (the cosmological hypothesis), but is also stripped of its existential weight, of the love of life, the absence of teleology, and the valuing of each moment for its own sake rather than for some future purpose.   So, coming back to the title's question: what is the intended target audience for this series? The genre's typical audience, younger, used to more cinematic and immediate storytelling like Final Fantasy, may find the excessive density boring, while a more cultured and patient audience might find the superficial name dropping of Nietzsche irritating. What's left, then, is a fairly patient niche that doesn't actually know the source material in depth, which is itself proof that the work fails to keep the promises implicitly made by its choice of subtitles.   The connection to Pokémon Ruby/Sapphire/Emerald stems from a similar problem, though of a different nature: those who have the age and patience to read carefully find the story dialogue (I don't mean the purely functional dialogue) mediocre enough to skip, so they don't read it by choice. Those who are too young to have developed that filter simply don't yet have the skills or patience to process that text. The result is that the story dialogue goes unread with any real attention by any age group. I found it almost funny that two works that are practically polar opposites end up sharing a similar problem, even if for entirely opposite reasons.   Coming back to Xenosaga, this isn't an isolated case but almost a structural flaw of the author's body of work, though far less severe in Xenogears, since that game doesn't use evocative subtitles (there is one misleading quote about the death of God), and different in nature in Xenoblade ( Xenoblade 2 Spoilers: which ties in similarly, for a story full of symbols and apparent complexity that nonetheless trivializes its own dramatic weight by bringing Pyra and Mythra back after ten minutes) .   Posted by u/Worth_Mail_3292 · [comments]
clusters.summary: User @Worth_Mail_3292 critiques the JRPG *Xenosaga* series for failing to deliver on the philosophical depth implied by its Nietzschean subtitles, arguing that the narrative offers only superficial name-dropping. The post analyzes how the series misinterprets key concepts like the "will to power," "Beyond Good and Evil," and "eternal recurrence," resulting in a story that is too dense for casual *Final Fantasy* fans but too shallow for serious philosophy enthusiasts. This structural flaw is compared to *Pokémon Ruby/Sapphire/Emerald*, where the dialogue is either skipped by experienced players or too complex for younger ones, leaving neither demographic engaged. The author also notes similar, though less severe, issues in creator Takahashi’s *Xenogears* and *Xenoblade 2*, concluding that the works promise a rigorous dialogue that they ultimately fail to provide.
